candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record points to autoimmune hepatitis as the most likely underlying cause (elevated IgG 2580 mg/dL, markedly elevated transaminases, negative viral/metabolic workup, negative autoantibodies notwithstanding—seronegative AIH is recognized). Acute liver failure is the resulting syndrome/complication, not the final diagnostic entity. C001 names the syndrome with its components but omits the etiologic diagnosis entirely.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Acute liver failure describes the clinical syndrome (coagulopathy, encephalopathy, hyperbilirubinemia) but does not identify the underlying etiology; the reference diagnosis is autoimmune hepatitis, which is the specific etiologic diagnosis requested

case_quality_flags: Seronegative autoimmune hepatitis scenario: all standard autoantibodies negative, diagnosis rests on elevated IgG, exclusion of other causes, and clinical context—biopsy not mentioned, which would normally be required for definitive AIH diagnosis
Dual HAV IgM positivity and prior HAV episode one month earlier may represent residual IgM rather than active infection; HEV seropositivity with undetectable RNA adds diagnostic complexity
